questions.prompt: Which of these count toward a Claude model's context window?

options.text: Only the user's latest message, plus the system prompt above it
options.explanation: Earlier turns, tool definitions and the output count too. On the API, previous turns are preserved completely.

options.text: Only the input; the output has its own separate limit
options.explanation: The Claude docs count the response inside the window, including extended thinking.

options.text: The system prompt, messages, tool definitions and the output
options.explanation: Right. The Claude docs say everything in the request counts, and so does the output the model generates.

questions.prompt: According to Anthropic, when can you skip RAG and send the whole knowledge base?

options.text: When it is smaller than about 200,000 tokens
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says that is about 500 pages, and prompt caching makes the approach faster and cheaper.

options.text: Never; long prompts always lose to retrieval
options.explanation: Anthropic says the simplest solution is sometimes the best: a small knowledge base can go in the prompt whole.

options.text: Whenever the model has a 1M-token window
options.explanation: Window size is not Anthropic's test. Its rule is the size of the knowledge base: under 200,000 tokens.

questions.prompt: What is context rot, per the Claude docs?

options.text: Cached prompts expire after five minutes
options.explanation: That is the default cache lifetime, a different topic. Context rot is about accuracy.

options.text: Accuracy and recall degrade as the token count grows
options.explanation: Right. That is why what you put in the context matters as much as how much fits.

options.text: Old messages are deleted automatically when the window is full
options.explanation: On the API, earlier turns are kept. Context rot is about the model using a long context less well.
